props.gloss_en: the mishna: a woman who discharges semen on the third day is impure
the mishna's source: 'be ready for three days' (Ex 19:15)
the mishna: one washes the circumcision on the third day that falls on Shabbat -- 'and it was on the third day, when they were in pain' (Gen 34:25)
the mishna's first clause (impure) is not R' Elazar b. Azarya's -- were it his, we heard him say 'pure'
the mishna's last clause (washing the circumcision) follows R' Elazar b. Azarya
he reads the first clause as 'pure'
and he sets the whole mishna as R' Elazar b. Azarya's
the first clause is the Rabbis'
REbA: a woman who discharges semen on the third day is pure
R' Yishmael: sometimes it is four onot, sometimes five, sometimes six
R' Akiva: always five onot; if part of the first ona passed, she is given part of the sixth
the Rabbis: [at Sinai] they made the separation on the fifth day
R' Yosei: they made the separation on the fourth day
granted, R' Elazar b. Azarya follows the Rabbis [of the Sinai separation]
and R' Yishmael follows R' Yosei
R' Akiva actually follows R' Yosei
Rav Adda bar Ahava: Moshe ascended [Sinai] early in the morning
...and descended early in the morning
he ascended early, as it is written 'and Moshe rose early in the morning and went up to Mount Sinai' (Ex 34:4)
he descended early, as it is written 'go, descend, and you shall ascend, you and Aaron with you' (Ex 19:24)
Rav Huna: Israel are holy and do not have relations by day
Rava: if it was a dark house, it is permitted
Rava (or Rav Pappa): a Torah scholar darkens [the room] with his cloak and it is permitted
Abaye bar Ravin and Rav Chanina bar Avin: the Torah was given to tevulei yom
Mareimar: [the teaching is that the Torah was] fit [to be given to tevulei yom], is what I say
R' Yitzchak: 'from the first I did not speak in secret' (Isa 48:16) -- [against receiving the Torah at twilight]
R' Yitzchak: so that these would not be going to receive the Torah while those were going to immerse -- [against immersing and receiving it on Shabbat morning]
these are R' Yishmael's and R' Akiva's words; but the Sages say six full onot are required
Rav Chisda: the dispute is where [the semen] left the woman
Rav Chisda: but where it left the man, it is impure as long as it is moist
the baraita: 'and every garment and every hide on which there is semen' (Lev 15:17) -- excluding semen that is foul
no: the baraita speaks of semen that left a woman

questions.gloss_en: Rav Pappa: Jewish semen in a gentile woman's body -- what is the law? Jews, who worry over mitzvot, have warm bodies, gentiles who do not, not; or perhaps, since they eat creeping things, their bodies are warm too? -- תיקו

Rav Pappa: and if you say [gentiles' bodies are warm too] -- in an animal's body, what is the law? a woman, who has a corridor, makes it foul, an animal, which has none, does not; or perhaps there is no difference? -- תיקו
